title: Hot-swap Attn Kernel Controller with Memory-aware Profiling
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Since integrating FlashAttention v2 and selectively enabling v3 builds for some GPU families, we've observed intermittent token-latency regressions and outlier memory spikes on long-prefill requests (seq_len >= 8192) for a subset of matrix shapes. Root cause signals point to suboptimal kernel paths chosen at runtime under specific tiling heuristics and failing heuristics for micro-batched prefill workloads. Purpose: Implement a Hot-swap Attn Kernel Controller that can: 1) dynamically profile micro-batches at connection startup and during warmup windows, 2) select per-request kernel candidates (v2, v3, fused hybrids) based on observed latency/memory tradeoffs, and 3) gracefully fallback or pin kernels per-client when regressions are detected. Scope: runtime inference serving only (prefill + decode), telemetry + lightweight profiler, kernel-mapping table, and rollout controls in the console (canary + force-pin). Non-goals: model conversion, upstream FA kernel source changes, or kernel authoring.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Controller chooses non-regressing kernel for >95% of sampled long-prefill requests in internal canary baseline; 2) No regression introduced to median token latency (<5% variance) across cross-GPU tests; 3) Telemetry exposes per-kernel latency/memory metrics in Console; 4) Runtime exposes a per-customer pin for kernel variant and an automatic rollback when error rate or latency SLO is breached.
tech_notes: Design: - Lightweight profiler (nanosecond granularity sampling) runs for first 100 requests or 30s warmup, whichever comes first. - Memory-aware decision uses estimated peak KV cache + observed allocator high watermark to avoid OOM paths in FAv3. - Hot-swap is implemented as a kernel-binding table keyed by (model-arch, dtype, seqlen-bucket, batchsize, GPU-arch). - Fallback policy: prefer v3 when latency/power-usage improves >=6% and memory headroom >= 12%; else prefer v2 or fused hybrid. - Add 'pin_kernel' flag on session creation API and Console rollout to lock variant. - Telemetry: add attn_kernel.variant, attn_kernel.latency_p50/p95, attn_kernel.peak_memory, attn_kernel.failures.
implementation_plan: 1) Prototype profiler + decision logic in an internal binary (Jonah) — 2 weeks. 2) Integrate hot-swap binding into runtime (Aisha) — 2 weeks. 3) Add Console rollout UI + API for pinning (PM + front-end) — 1 week. 4) Canary on staging with 5 customers and synthetic workloads (bench-suite attached) — 1 week. 5) Gradual rollout with observability gates and auto-rollback heuristics — 2 weeks.

risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Hot-swap churn could increase jitter during warmup windows. Mitigation: gate hot-swap behind a warmup commit window and use conservative thresholds; add jitter dampening and require >10 samples before switching. Risk: Telemetry cost. Mitigation: sample 1% of low-priority requests and full telemetry for canary sessions.
test_plan: - Unit tests for mapping logic and decision thresholds. - Integration tests with flashattention v2/v3 docker images on A100 and H100. - Synthetic long-prefill suite (seq_len 4096/8192/16384) across batch sizes [1,2,4,8]. - Regression verification against ENG-4721 baseline traces. - Post-rollout A/B comparing token cost and p95 latency for 48h windows.
